planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in humus-rich, well-drained, evenly moist soil in dappled to full shade in spring, siting out of drying winter wind in the coldest part of its range.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained, consistently moist soil in dappled or full shade, working in compost at planting and mulching to keep roots cool. Unlike its purely tropical relatives, this species tolerates real winter cold, surviving into the upper single digits once established, which makes it one of the few schefflera options for outdoor, in-ground planting well outside the tropics. Each glossy, dark green leaf is divided into narrow, radiating leaflets on an upright, multi-stemmed shrub that builds slowly into a bold architectural specimen valued for its year-round evergreen texture beneath tree canopies. Shelter young plants from harsh winter wind and hard freezes for the first few seasons while the root system establishes.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade in spring, choosing a sheltered site protected from drying wind and the harshest winter cold.

directions: Plant in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, providing shelter from cold, drying winds while the plant establishes over its first few winters. This large, coarse-textured shrub carries deeply lobed, felted, dark bronze-green leaves that emerge with a distinctive silvery down, giving way to upright, branched panicles of small cream-white flowers in autumn when little else is blooming in the shade garden. It is among the more cold-tolerant schefflera species available, allowing outdoor woodland planting in warm-temperate gardens rather than restricting it to a container or greenhouse. Prune to shape or to remove any winter dieback in spring, and mulch well to protect the root zone through cold snaps.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society — Schefflera delavayi (Award of Garden Merit)
Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh — Flora of China notes

planting.note: Root stem-tip cuttings or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained, average potting mix or garden soil in partial shade to bright indirect light in spring.

directions: Root stem-tip cuttings or grow container specimens in well-drained, average potting mix in partial shade or bright indirect light indoors. This naturally dwarf, tight-jointed sport of the standard dwarf umbrella tree stays noticeably smaller and denser without pruning, forming a compact mound of small, glossy, dark green umbrella-shaped leaflets well suited to tabletop pots, dish gardens, and tight indoor corners where the species form would quickly outgrow its space. Pinch new growth occasionally to keep the bushy habit tidy, and rotate the pot regularly indoors for even, symmetrical growth. Keep out of cold drafts and allow the soil surface to dry slightly between waterings.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center
